Slicing Maelstrom is cast once (0.25s cast time) to start the storm
storm strikes bolts every 0.5s for 3s, each a separate damage instance with a per-hit ramp
each subsequent bolt a target has taken deals 10% more damage, capped at 150% of the initial bolt's damage
Lightning Rush is a ghosted form that blocks basic attacks while active
E can be manually recast after 0.5s or auto-recasts after its 2s duration; cooldown starts post-effect
recasting E grants bonus attack speed for 4s, extendable by 1s per crit up to the original duration
the recast's bonus attack speed is allowed to exceed the normal attack speed cap
basic attacks generate a stack of Electrical Surge up to a cap of 4
the attack that reaches 4 stacks is empowered
the 4th basic attack consumes all stacks to deal bonus magic on-hit damage (can crit) and apply a Mark of the Storm stack

needsBespoke.why: Mark of the Storm is a stack system shared across all four abilities (Q, W-active, E, R) plus, ambiguously, basic attacks: any ability hit adds/refreshes a stack on the target (cap 3, 6s duration), and the 3rd stack self-consumes to stun and restore 25 energy, with a 6s diminishing-return window per target. This is a cross-ability target-stack counter with a trigger effect (stun+resource) that the closed primitive list's single-ability target-stacks primitive does not capture on its own; it needs to be modeled as one shared counter fed by multiple sources with a proc effect and its own separate 'stack immunity' rule when triggered by R specifically. Additionally, W's active has a hard precondition (a nearby marked target or being inside R's radius) to even be castable, which is a bespoke castability gate rather than a simple conditional-damage modifier.

unsettled.question: Do Kennen's plain (unempowered) basic attacks apply a stack of Mark of the Storm, or only his abilities (Q/E/R) and the 4-stack-empowered W attack?
options: Only Q, E, R casts and the Electrical Surge-empowered 4th attack apply Mark of the Storm stacks; ordinary basic attacks do not
All basic attacks apply Mark of the Storm stacks in addition to abilities, since the passive tooltip calls out 'abilities' broadly and on-hit sources are often included
quotes: {{sbc|Innate:}} '''Kennen's''' {{tip|abilities}} apply a {{tip|stack}} of ''Mark of the Storm'' to enemies hit for 6 seconds

unsettled.question: Does the Electrical Surge stack-consuming (4th) attack itself also generate a fresh Electrical Surge stack, or does the counter reset to 0 and require 4 more attacks before the next empowered attack?
options: The empowering attack consumes stacks and does not add a new one; next empowered attack requires 4 more attacks (period of 4)
The consuming attack also generates a stack simultaneously, effectively shortening the cycle
quotes: At 4 stacks, his next basic attack {{tip|on-attack}} consumes all stacks to both deal {{as|'''bonus''' magic damage}} and apply a stack of ''{{ai|Mark of the Storm|Kennen}}'' {{tip|on-hit}}

unsettled.question: During Slicing Maelstrom, do the periodic bolt strikes (every 0.5s) each count as a separate 'ability hit' for Mark of the Storm purposes, meaning the passive stun could trigger repeatedly (every 1.5s) throughout R's 3s duration on a stationary target?
options: Yes, each R tick applies/refreshes a Mark of the Storm stack like any other ability hit, so the passive stun can trigger mid-R
No, R's DoT ticks are excluded from Mark of the Storm application and only the initial cast (or none of R) applies a stack
quotes: After {{ai|Slicing Maelstrom|Kennen}} applies its third stack, the target gains a 6-second stack immunity against ''Slicing Maelstrom'' that refreshes on subsequent hits.

proposal: Pre-fight: max Q first, then take W/E per standard order, take R at level 6 and whenever available thereafter.
Open with Q (Thundering Shuriken) on the dummy for upfront magic damage and to apply a Mark of the Storm stack.
Auto-attack to build Electrical Surge stacks while Q is on cooldown.
Cast E (Lightning Rush) to pass through the dummy for its magic damage, apply another Mark of the Storm stack, and restore 40 energy.
If a Mark of the Storm stack is present (from Q/E) and W is off cooldown, cast W (Electrical Surge active) for AoE magic damage and another mark application.
Once R is available (level 6+), cast R to start the storm's periodic bolt damage and bonus resists (resists irrelevant to the damage fight), continuing to auto-attack and weave Q/E/W on cooldown.

Recast E (or let it auto-recast) as soon as it has dealt its damage, since a single stationary target is hit only once regardless of dash duration, in order to gain the bonus attack speed sooner and exceed the attack speed cap for more autos.
Weave basic attacks continuously between spell casts so the 4th attack consumes Electrical Surge stacks for its bonus on-hit magic damage as often as possible.

Whenever the passive's 3rd Mark of the Storm stack lands on the dummy, take the free stun window as an opportunity to land more autos/casts (the stun itself does not need modeling as CC, but the accompanying 25 energy restore should be tracked to sustain the energy-cost rotation).
questions: Should E be recast immediately (0.5s) for earliest attack-speed uptime, or held for its full 2s duration for any reason relevant to the dummy fight?

Is it worth delaying W's active cast to wait for a mark from Q/E, or can R's radius alone satisfy W's cast precondition for the whole duration of R, letting W be cast off cooldown regardless of Q/E landing?

In the 15s window, is it optimal to hold R until near the end (to maximize DoT ramp uptime given its 120s cooldown means it casts once) or open with it early to front-load more of the fight under its bolts?
